problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S={1,2}\times (-1,1)$ in the Cartesian plane?
worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B={(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B}
$$

In this case, the set 

$$
S={1,2}\times (-1,1)
$$

contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is either $1$ or $2$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $(-1,1).$

$$
S={(x,y)\,:\,x\in {1,2},\,y\in (-1,1)}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider ${S}_{1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $1$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $(-1,1).$

$$
{S}_{1}={(1,y)\,:\,y\in (-1,1)}
$$

This set is represented by the line segment shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/11522acdfeaad022847fedbcf6052424216587f99f2691e80ed96152f30818a4.png)

Next, consider ${S}_{2}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $2$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $(-1,1).$

$$
{S}_{2}={(2,y)\,:\,y\in (-1,1)}.
$$

This set is represented by the line segment shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/90b6a9c00d366e4a03c8c974476fdf06bc9fa73c9c26e9a0cd6ba9a4bda8e66d.png)

Our Cartesian product is the *union* of these subsets:

$$
S={S}_{1}\cup {S}_{2}
$$

Therefore, $S$ can be represented by the two line segments shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040430/assets/bbf0d5ecc57bc30c7a3f4db7a1d30b27633e4586b2768e315715df72ce41333f.png)
